hints: Focus on what else is formed besides the salt in each case, an acid plus a carbonate, a reactive metal, or an alkali behave very differently.
Remember that butanoic acid with sodium carbonate gives off carbon dioxide, and with sodium metal gives off hydrogen.
Check which reaction makes only water as the second product, with no bubbles or gas evolved, and exclude it from your list.
walkthrough:
**Recall the three ways to make a carboxylate salt**

All three reagents will neutralise butanoic acid to give sodium butanoate. The question asks for salt plus a gas, so we must look at the other product.

General idea:
$$\text{acid + base / carbonate / metal} \rightarrow \text{salt + other product}$$

**Test reaction 1 and reaction 2 for gas**

Carbonates always release carbon dioxide with acids, and reactive metals release hydrogen with acids. Both count as gases at room temperature.

$$2\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COOH} + \text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COONa} + \text{CO}_{2} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}$$
$$2\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COONa} + \text{H}_{2}$$

**Test reaction 3 for gas**

Hydroxide neutralisation of a carboxylic acid gives salt plus water only. Water is a liquid, not a gas, so no effervescence is seen.

$$\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COONa} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}$$
So only 1 and 2 give salt plus gas.

options.A: Incorrect. This option includes 1, 2 and 3. While 1 and 2 are correct, 3 gives sodium butanoate plus water only, with no gas evolved, so 3 must be excluded.
options.B: Correct. Reaction 1 gives sodium butanoate plus carbon dioxide gas, and reaction 2 gives sodium butanoate plus hydrogen gas. Reaction 3 gives only water, so 1 and 2 only is the right combination.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes 2 and 3. Reaction 2 is correct as it gives hydrogen, but reaction 3 is neutralisation to give water, not a gas, and it misses out reaction 1 which correctly gives carbon dioxide.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes 1 only. Reaction 1 is correct as it gives carbon dioxide, but it wrongly leaves out reaction 2 which also gives a gas, hydrogen, with sodium metal.
